en: The Hymn to the Lion of the Śākyas composed by Brahmā. Homage to the Lord of the Śākyas!

Homage be to you, Lord of the World, King of the Śākyas, the sun to the lotus of the True Dharma; to you who have struck down the host of enemies that are the afflictions, with the lamps of perfect enlightenment having destroyed the web of delusion. (1)

That infinite Dharma-knowledge, which cannot be attained even by hosts of Brahman-sages, royal sages, and celestial sages with their many jewels, has been attained by you— by means of which you shall indeed bring about the destruction of the entire host of Daityas.

Homage be to you, the Lord of the three worlds, by whom the wheel of the sublime Dharma was set in motion, at which the earth— with its oceans and king of mountains— trembled incessantly as if filled with joy.
In that [place], winds endowed with the three qualities blew from the sky, and rains fell; there were flowers of various colors and fragrant water. Homage be to you, the sole Lord of the world! (4)

Namuci, who was invincible by others and surrounded by the most excellent armies numbering hundreds of millions, was conquered by you alone, unarmed; homage be to you, the treader upon the powerful! (5)

Obeisance to you, the sole Lord of the world, who by nature brings about the end of birth and old age, and who was born blazing with that illusory power (*māyā*) in order to protect the three worlds. 6.

In order to cause that conduct of awakening—the bridge to liberation—to blossom throughout the worlds of the three realms, you took birth among mortals while residing in Tuṣita; homage be to you, O King of Supreme Awakening!

Homage be to you, whose great vow is sublime! Having undertaken a perfect vow, it is for that purpose that you have come to the world of mortals, so that the multitude of beings may be sent forth toward the city of liberation.
And whoever, standing before the foremost of the Śākyas, shall recite this most meritorious *Aṣṭaka* composed by Brahmā,
will cast off suffering and the fear of great sins, and go joyfully to the city of Śrīghana.
The hymn to the illustrious Śākyasiṃha composed by Brahmā is completed.
